extracted.intended_audience: external and internal peer reviewers asked to review book proposals, sample chapters, or full manuscripts for Springer Nature (books & proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for experts reviewing book proposals, sample chapters, or complete manuscripts for Springer Nature, covering whether to accept an invitation, how to assess content and integrity, and how to write constructive reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting research integrity / follow COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers play a vital role in ensuring the content we publish is robust, ethical and free from misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature follows COPE and asks reviewers to follow COPE's Ethical Guidelines for Peer-reviewers to safeguard research integrity; help identify misconduct and report concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting invitation — Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you familiar with the specific topic covered in the proposal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not familiar with the topic, inform the publisher rather than accepting; you have been invited because the publisher believes you are an expert in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting invitation — Time / meeting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you meet the review deadline?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accept if you can meet the deadline; missing the deadline may mean feedback is too late to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting invitation — Competing interest / conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any issues that may affect your ability to give a fair and impartial review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider financial interests, personal opinions on the topic, or personal/professional relationships with the author(s)/editor(s). If in doubt, discuss potential conflicts with the publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting invitation — Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Book proposals, sample materials and manuscripts under review are highly confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not discuss the material with others without prior consent from the publisher; follow the publisher's peer review policy on confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — no plagiarism or misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: You should never plagiarize the content or ideas presented in the review materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use information in the manuscript to make business decisions (e.g., buying/selling stock). Follow the Book Peer Reviewers' Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct — do not use AI tools
rubrics_metrics.description: You should not use AI tools when reviewing the materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are selected for their human expertise; the value in reviewing is human judgement. See publisher policy for latest on AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine type of peer review (anonymity model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand whether the review is single-anonymous or double-anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-anonymous: reviewer knows authors/editors; double-anonymous: neither party knows the other. Refer to invitation to know which approach is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship — author/editor expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the author(s)/editor(s) have the expertise to write this book?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the qualifications and track record of the authors/editors relative to the book's subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship — diversity (especially edited volumes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the book have a diverse authorship?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For edited volumes in particular, diversity across contributors is important; consider geographic, institutional, demographic, and intellectual diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship — representation of region/community
rubrics_metrics.description: If the book is describing a particular region or community, does the authorship include authors from that region/community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether local/regional perspectives are represented appropriately by authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book title accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the title accurately say what the book is about?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise if the title is misleading or does not reflect the scope and emphasis of the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents — chapter appropriateness and logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the chapters appropriate and logical? Are there topics out of place or missing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate organization, sequencing, and whether key topics are included or redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the content suitable for the intended audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess level, tone, and scope relative to the stated target readership; suggest adjustments if mismatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with series scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If the book is intended for a specific book series, does the material fit with the scope of the series?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider series aims and readership when judging fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of coverage (for sample content/full manuscripts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the author(s)/editor(s) adequately covered the topic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify gaps in coverage or areas requiring expansion to make the work comprehensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the material well written? Do you have any concerns about the author(s)/editor(s)’s writing abilities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on clarity, structure, readability, and suitability of prose for the audience; point out examples and suggest improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and citation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the author(s)/editor(s) cite relevant materials?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for up-to-date, appropriate, and sufficiently broad referencing; flag missing key works or over-reliance on certain sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions — assessing resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you initially reviewed the proposal, has your feedback been sufficiently addressed by the author(s)/editor(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On re-review, focus on issues you raised and whether they have been addressed; if not, evaluate the authors' reasons fairly and explain remaining significant issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting author manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for unusual or suspicious authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag concerns about inappropriate attribution, ghost authorship, or other manipulations of authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting citation manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for questionable references or over-citation of the author(s)/editor(s)’ own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify patterns that suggest citation padding or self-citation intended to bias apparent impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting AI-generated content / 'tortured phrases'
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify text strings that sound reasonable but have no true meaning or are pure nonsense; unnatural phrasing used in place of recognized terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag suspected AI-generated passages (including 'tortured phrases') and report concerns to the publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you believe any of the content to have been plagiarized?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected plagiarism as part of safeguarding research integrity and follow COPE/publisher procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write constructive reviews — start with positives
rubrics_metrics.description: Your review should be constructive and aimed at helping the author(s)/editor(s) improve their proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin by highlighting strengths before addressing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write constructive reviews — provide examples and specific suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific in your feedback and suggest improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a chapter lacks depth, suggest specific areas to expand; offer concrete examples and additional references where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write constructive reviews — avoid personal attacks and be respectful
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid personal attacks: be respectful and objective in your criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the work rather than the author; maintain professional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write constructive reviews — offer additional resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest further references that might improve the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend relevant literature, datasets, or conceptual frameworks to strengthen the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write constructively — be fair and recognise limits of expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Be fair: recognize where your expertise may be limited and recommend additional reviews if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If out of your depth on particular topics, state this and suggest who else might be suitable to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report structure — separate confidential editor comments and author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviewer report should be divided into two parts: Comments for the Publishing Editor and Comments for the author(s)/editor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide confidential recommendations (accept, revise, reject) to the editor and detailed, constructive feedback for authors/editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review follow-up on resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If resubmitted materials require further review, focus on the issues you raised and whether they have been addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If significant issues remain unresolved, explain why further changes are necessary; evaluate authors' responses fairly.
